14: That there is a distinction - a distinction in its "ways", namely, that in this way it is like that thing, and in this way it is not alike.  Such as, in our Mishnah, "in three ways" -- to exclude [betrothal through the] marriage canopy, which does not serve to acquire. Regarding the zav: it is thus [i.e., one of the seven ways] which is considered circumstances beyond one's control regarding the laws of zav, but not any other type of circumstance beyond one's control [which one would not be penalized for regarding other laws]. Regarding bills of divorce: in these ways they are like [bills of manumission], but not where one says "give this bill of divorce to my wife" or "this bill of manumission to my slave", since one may retract a bill of divorce but not a manumission, since one may act in a person’s interests in his absence.
Is also precise - that where there are no distinctions, [as in the opinion of Rabbi Eliezer], the Mishnah uses expression "with regard to every matter."
